output.name: Varosk
output.myth: Varosk was the coat Ennu the Kite-Wright sewed for a fisher named Mot, from goat-gut and pine tar, so thick the sea ran off it like rain off a roof. Mot wore it into every squall and came home dry. Tavo saw this and was jealous, for nothing of his kept anything dry. So one night he came down on the boat with his whole breath. That same week the gale stove in Rathun, the Holed Ketch, like a bad crate. Mot went over the rail. The coat held the sea out, and held it out, and held Mot in. Nobody bails a coat. The water stayed outside and the man stayed inside, and the coat carried him out past the broken stern of Rathun and toward Halun, the Kite for the Drowned Child, where a mother ties a small kite and writes the name in the knots. Kael has cast for him every night since and never once caught him. Hesk counts the buttons and has not yet agreed the number is right. Mot is up there still, a little dry, looking for the way home.
output.finding: Find Rathun, the Holed Ketch, then look one fist (about 10°) due east of it to find Varosk.
